title: The PR renames all five readiness states, which is a room-mind change canon never approved
detail: COPY_STANDARD §17 and the map replace the five canon state names everywhere they appear on the page. Canon §4.17 locks these gate-based states as primitives, and §13 says user-facing copy names the state itself ('You're Building / Inheritable with guardrails / Hire-ready'). The page's L592-596 and L1102-1106 leaves copy those cockpit gates word for word. The new names also change what the states mean. 'Partially documented' claims a documentation test, but canon's Building gate measures activity ('activity exists but the next hire would still be improvising'; ≥2 parts ≥8/20). The PR changes no canon file (commit 3fb1ed7 touches only the four COPY_* files) and never cites CLAUDE.md, so it skips Part IV §4 (name the mind issue, propose it, get founder confirmation, update §4.17, then change the face). CODEX_HANDOFF.md:45 also tells the implementer to hunt down 'you are the system' and 'inheritable' as defects.

recommendation: Revert the page to the canon state names (the page can add a plain one-line gloss under each, which §13's teach-on-first-use exception allows). If the founder wants the new names, it becomes a §4.17 mind change: get approval, then update canon, VERDICT_LABEL, ClimbDrawer and cockpit together, and drop the 'documented' wording unless a gate actually measures documentation.

COPY_STANDARD §17 (L404-424) asks for the new names, and CODEX_HANDOFF.md:45 lists 'you are the system' and 'inheritable' as validation terms. Commit 3fb1ed7 adds only the 4 COPY_* files, and none of them mentions CLAUDE.md or canon. 'Partially documented' misstates the Building gate, which measures activity, not documentation.

title: Future Autopsy (a protected room) is rewritten as 'Deal risk analysis', the exact softening canon forbids
detail: Canon §4.14 says Future Autopsy must never be softened into 'risk review'. §5 protects the room from being made generic, renamed, or watered down. The PR's card lead is now 'Deal risk analysis.' The room description becomes 'Projects deal-loss risk before the deal is lost.', which drops the written autopsy: the causal-pattern story told before the deal dies, which is one of the room's primitives. The source of this is COPY_STANDARD §4, which lets the name survive only 'if its surrounding copy says explicitly that it projects deal-loss risk.' That makes the protected name conditional and requires risk-review framing. CODEX_HANDOFF.md:45 also lists 'autopsy' and 'dies' as terms to remove.
evidence: U167 O 'The autopsy, early. It writes the story of how the deal dies before it does, names the pattern, and routes you to the room where the fix happens.' → R 'Deal risk analysis. Antaeus projects how the deal is likely to fail, identifies the recurring risk pattern, and links to the workflow where you can address it.'; U197 'It writes how the deal dies before it does.'→'Projects deal-loss risk before the deal is lost.'; COPY_STANDARD.md:96. Canon CLAUDE.md:297-304 (§4.14 'Never soften into "risk review."'; primitives include 'causal-pattern narrative'), :445 (§5).
recommendation: Keep the forensic framing: lead with 'Future Autopsy' or the plain 'The autopsy, written early', and say it writes how this deal is likely to die, names the failure pattern, and routes you to the fix. Delete the §4 conditional rule from COPY_STANDARD and take 'autopsy' and 'dies' off the handoff's banned-term list.
skeptic_reasoning: Confirmed. U167 now leads with 'Deal risk analysis.', and U197 becomes 'Projects deal-loss risk before the deal is lost.', which drops the 'writes how the deal dies' story. COPY_STANDARD.md:96 makes the name conditional on risk-projection copy. CLAUDE.md:304 says 'Never soften into "risk review."' One overstatement: the room label 'Future Autopsy' survives on the all-rooms card (U196, action=keep), so the name itself is not removed, only the card lead and descriptions. The handoff's line 45 lists 'autopsy/dies' as terms to validate, with proper names allowed, not as outright bans. The core violation of the protected room still stands.

title: The locked Signal Console attention bands and the heat concept are replaced with generic priority labels
detail: Signal Console is a protected room (§5). Its locked 2026-07-02 face sorts accounts into four bands: act now / reach while warm / emerging / going cold. Heat is canon's measured account quantity: §2 defines Account as having 'signals, heat', and §4.7 gives the heat formula. The shipped app uses these labels verbatim: src/signal-console/v4/lib/attention.ts:25 has now = 'Act now', why 'hot, and something just moved', and cold = 'Going cold', why 'was warm, now quiet'. COPY_STANDARD §3 treats hot/warm/cold as metaphors to strip. So U31, which quoted the shipped band exactly, becomes 'High priority · recent company change'. U83's 'going cold' becomes 'have had no recent activity', which loses the meaning 'was warm, now quiet': an account that was never touched also has no recent activity. In U36 and U73, 'running hot' becomes 'Antaeus ranks Chomps highly because…', which removes heat from the explanation entirely.
evidence: U30 O 'Act now, reach while they’re warm, emerging, going cold.' → R 'See which accounts need action now, which have new signals, and which have had no recent activity.'; U31 'Act now — hot, and something just moved'→'High priority · recent company change'; U83 '…three going cold'→'…three have had no recent activity'; COPY_STANDARD.md:69. Canon CLAUDE.md:117/§2 Account row, :227 (§4.7 heat formula), :445 (§5), :1699 (2026-07-02 Signal Console LOCKED bands).
recommendation: Keep the four band names as the room's labels and add a plain gloss where needed (e.g. 'Going cold — was active, now quiet'). Keep heat as a named product quantity. Remove hot/warm/cold from COPY_STANDARD §3 for this room, or update canon first if the founder wants the bands renamed.
skeptic_reasoning: The band part is confirmed. src/signal-console/v4/lib/attention.ts BAND_META has now='Act now'/'hot, and something just moved' and cold='Going cold'/'was warm, now quiet'. The source's L637 copies the shipped band exactly, and U31 rewrites it to 'High priority · recent company change'. U30 collapses the four bands into three phrases, and U83 turns 'going cold' into 'no recent activity', which loses 'was warm'. The heat part is overstated: the page never uses the word 'heat' (grep finds only 'running hot' at L655 and L927), so the page has no named heat quantity to lose, only the metaphor. Downgraded from high.

title: The page still says its screens are real, but the PR relabels those screens so they no longer match the shipped app
detail: The PR keeps the footnote claim that the screens show the real product with sample data. It also changes UI labels inside those screens that exist verbatim in shipped code. Examples: 'Pain & consequence' (DiscoveryStudioV4.tsx:81); 'One thing to notice' and 'N of 7 parts ready' (FoundingGtmV4.tsx:73,150); 'The circle — who's hands-on' (PilotDeskV4.tsx:260); 'Your line' and 'The one thing blocking' (GettingToSignedV4.tsx:227,236,291); 'the machine' as a Live Edge tag (LiveEdge.tsx:250); the readiness gates and the Signal Console bands (see those findings). Canon §2 says a room may enrich a noun but not redefine it, and Part IV §4 says renaming shipped product states needs founder approval. So each relabel is either a false claim on the page or an unapproved app change. Some divergences go the other way: the shipped Dashboard still says 'The most valuable move on your board' (DashboardV4.tsx:112), which breaks §13's ban on 'move'. In those cases the PR's wording is canon-correct and the app is the one that needs fixing.
evidence: U333 R 'Screens throughout this page show real product areas with sample data.'; U45/U140 'Pain & consequence · live'→'Problem and business impact · live'; U58/U78 'One thing to notice —'→'Pattern:'; U52/U156 'Who is hands-on'→'Active pilot participants'; U162 'The relay'→'Referral path'; leaf 'Your line'→'Your position'. Canon CLAUDE.md:126-130 (§2 rules for nouns), :1327-1341 (Part IV §4).
recommendation: Sort each relabel into one of two buckets. Where the page label is canon-correct and the app is not (the 'move' labels), fix the app. Where the relabel contradicts canon (states, bands, segment names, 'one thing to notice', 'your line', 'the circle', 'the machine'), revert the page to the shipped label. Otherwise soften the footnote so it no longer promises verbatim screens.
skeptic_reasoning: Mostly confirmed. U333 still claims 'Screens throughout this page show real product areas with sample data'. The relabels do diverge from shipped strings: 'Pain & consequence' (DiscoveryStudioV4.tsx:81), 'One thing to notice' and 'parts ready' (FoundingGtmV4.tsx:73,150), 'Your line' and 'The one thing blocking' (GettingToSignedV4.tsx:227,236,291), and the readiness gates and bands. Two cited examples are inaccurate. 'the machine' never appears on the page; the original Live Edge copy said 'the system', so the PR's 'Antaeus' does not relabel a shipped tag the page showed. 'The relay' is not a user-facing string in shipped code (CallInAFavorV4.tsx:209 is a JSX comment and :242 is a CSS class). The 'move' point (DashboardV4.tsx:112) is correct. Largely an aggregation of the other findings, so medium rather than high.

title: Setup copy turns the operator's judgment work into 'entering information', the data-entry framing §12 forbids
detail: Canon Part III §12 (the heavy-seeding doctrine) and §4.3 Onboarding frame setup as authorship: 'It's authorship, not data entry'; 'they bring judgment, the app brings depth'; the setup is an asset that pays back every morning; 'we never apologize for the work'. The PR swaps the thinking for data entry across the page: 'entering the sales knowledge', 'founder input', 'information only you know', 'Document the sales process once', 'asks you to enter that context'. title: COPY_STANDARD bans the words canon uses for its settled voice and pushes demo copy into the machine narration canon forbids
detail: COPY_STANDARD §9 bans 'sees, notices, knows, wakes, remembers, hands you'. Its §3 table maps 'awake'→'configured and actively processing data' and 'in your head'→'undocumented founder knowledge'. Canon's own settled copy uses these words. §1's emotional target is 'this system sees what is actually happening'. The Welcome landing is 'the workspace is awake' (§4.1, shipped at WelcomeV4.tsx:25). Meanwhile §9's preferred verbs (reviews, analyzes, ranks, compares) produce exactly what §13 bans for UI and mockups: 'never narrate the machine… the user hears what is true… never how the system arrived at it.' Inside the Dashboard mockup, the plain fact 'Reaching out is the part of your motion furthest behind' becomes 'Antaeus ranks outreach as your least-completed sales activity'. §13's read-aloud plainness test also favors 'in your head' over 'undocumented founder knowledge'. By the authority order, CLAUDE.md outranks COPY_STANDARD.
evidence: U305 'One afternoon, and the workspace is awake…'→'Setup takes about one afternoon. The next morning, Antaeus ranks…' (dropping 'move' is correct; dropping 'awake' contradicts §4.1); U202 'What the system saw while you were out.'→'Workspace changes detected while you were away.'; U21 R 'Antaeus ranks outreach as your least-completed sales activity.' (in-product card); U36/U73 R 'Antaeus ranks Chomps highly because…'; U99 'A spreadsheet and what you remember'→'Spreadsheet + undocumented founder knowledge'; COPY_STANDARD.md:76-77, :208-240. Canon CLAUDE.md:86, :162-170, :406-410, :1188-1197, :979-1027 (§11 read-aloud test).
recommendation: Remove COPY_STANDARD §9 and the 'awake' and 'in your head' rows, or subordinate them to canon §11/§13. In product mockups, state the fact plainly without saying 'Antaeus ranks X because'. If the founder wants a no-personification rule, amend canon §1 and §4.1 first.

The shipped WelcomeV4.tsx:25 says 'the workspace is awake' (canon §4.1). Inside the dashboard mockup card, U21 becomes 'Antaeus ranks outreach as your least-completed sales activity', and U36/U73 become 'Antaeus ranks Chomps highly because…'. That is the machine narration §13 forbids in UI and mockups. U99 becomes 'Spreadsheet + undocumented founder knowledge', and U202 becomes 'Workspace changes detected while you were away.' title: Briefing and hero copy describe a morning review job and pilot-adoption checks that don't exist
detail:
Several rewrites describe what the product reviews and when, and get both wrong.

What runs: the heartbeat, every 30 minutes, for workspaces with data. It has four SQL generators:
- deal_decay: a deal has sat in the same stage for ≥7 days with no future-dated next step.
- signal_decay: a watched account has had no public signal for ≥14 days.
- proof_staleness: a pilot is past its readout window with no recorded outcome.
- discovery_rhythm: fewer than 1 call logged in 7 days.
There is no morning job. The Briefing world pipeline runs weekly (Monday 06:00 UTC). The Dashboard ranking is computed when the page opens. Nothing sends notifications.

Mismatches:
- #17 says "Each morning, Antaeus reviews your accounts, deals, calls, and sales activity and tells you". The heartbeat never reads outreach (sequences), and nothing is pushed to the user.
- #95 lists "accounts without recent engagement" (actually: no new public signals) and "pilots with low participant adoption". No adoption generator exists anywhere; the pilot check is about a missed readout.
- #203 says "generated each morning". Observations are generated every 30 minutes.
- #90 says "below your planned weekly activity". The floor is a fixed MIN_CALLS_PER_WEEK = 1, not the user's plan. The CTA was also changed to "Review a call", but the read is asking the user to hold calls.
- #305 says "The next morning, Antaeus ranks…". The onboarding landing hands back the first action immediately, so this is an underclaim.

#96 ("Every 30 minutes Antaeus reviews the latest workspace data") and #85 are accurate.

title: The reasons given for ranking Chomps first aren't what the ranking engine uses

- Trigger type is not an input, so "hiring trigger" is not a factor. Heat is.
